# AI migrations

> Case studies of software migrations done with AI: what worked, what failed, and which part AI did versus rule-based tools and people. Lessons drawn from them by aspect (planning, testing, review, rollout, cost and more), and a before-you-migrate checklist an agent runs on a repository.

Unofficial; company names describe the subject only. Every lesson comes from migrations; many apply to large engineering work done with AI agents generally. A lesson's "Old system as oracle" tag says whether its evidence leaned on the old system; it hints at how far the lesson travels but is not a filter, so judge each lesson by its own words. Each case says how far its claims can be checked and what stake its author has in the tools: weigh it accordingly; a lesson that rests only on cases whose authors sell the tool is never rated strong.

With a specific or a new model: process lessons (model ability: no) apply as they are. Start with the lessons tagged yes or partly whose cases name your model or its family ("By model" in lessons/index.md); treat those from other models as things to re-check on yours, not tips. A model released after the newest case (published 2026-11-03) has no evidence here yet. The lessons hold only what the cases show: no prompting advice.

"May be outdated" marks a lesson about what models can or cannot do (tagged "Depends on model ability: yes") whose most recent case (the later of its publication date and the end of its work) is more than 12 months older than the newest update in the log: newer models may no longer behave so; re-check it against recent work before you rely on it. Marked now: TOL-2, AGF-8. A lesson's Era gives the years of its cases and the newest model family among them.

Disclosure: the cases and lessons are drafted by Claude, an Anthropic model, and reviewed by the maintainer. At least 16 of the 24 cases used Claude models or Claude Code (Bloomberg, Ping.gg, GitHub, Checkly, Intel, Bun, GitLab, Mindstone, Datadog, Lutz Leonhardt, PagerDuty, Ladybird, Christopher Chedeau, Spotify, Robert Marshall, Slack; 6 others leave the models unstated), and Anthropic owns Bun, the subject of one case. GitHub, Intel, Mindstone and Ping.gg also used other vendors' models; where a source compares outcomes by model, that is its author's own unaudited report, and no lesson ranks vendors.

## How to use

- Before a migration or a large restructuring: run the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/checklist.md) on the repository and change nothing. Each question has a Check to measure and cites lesson IDs; open only the lessons and cases behind a gap.
- Lessons, one route: read [lessons/evidence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/evidence.md) (about 41 KB, the only file besides llms-full.txt that lists every lesson: one line each with tags, strength, cases and the cases against), then open an aspect page only for the lessons you use. For a large piece of AI-driven work that is not a migration (README "Learning from the lessons"), follow [docs/applying-lessons.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/applying-lessons.md).
- Open a case only when you need its detail. Each has "Who did what", "How it was checked", a Numbers table with the basis of each number, "What went wrong" and "Practices to copy". File format: [docs/case-format.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/case-format.md).
- Once a prediction has met a real event (a decision not to migrate, a regression, an item proven or failing at a revisit): tell what the checklist or the lessons foresaw and what they missed, in a field report ([how](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/docs/field-reports.md)); show the user the exact text before posting.
- Revisit: the newest update is "2026-11-14 — third update". If your record names it and no item is due for re-check (due: waiting or open, with commits in the project since the record's date), stop. Else, for each [log.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/log.md) entry newer than your record's, read changes/<entry>.md (newest: [2026-11-14-third-update](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/changes/2026-11-14-third-update.md)), the lesson IDs and questions it added, changed or removed.
- Relative links inside these files resolve against the raw URL of the file that holds them (under https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/).

## Lessons

The aspect pages (tag counts per page: [lessons/index.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/index.md)). Choose lessons in [lessons/evidence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/evidence.md) first; open a page only for the lessons you use.

- [Planning and scoping](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/planning.md): 13 lessons, PLN-n. How to size, slice, order and stage a large piece of AI-driven work before agents touch the code.
- [Testing and oracles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/testing.md): 15 lessons, TST-n. What tells you the new code is right, and where those oracles fail.
- [Verification loops and gates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/verification.md): 12 lessons, VER-n. The automated checks around each agent change, and what they can and cannot prove.
- [Code review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/review.md): 11 lessons, REV-n. How agent-written changes were reviewed, by agents and by people.
- [Release and rollout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/rollout.md): 11 lessons, ROL-n. How the new code reached users, and how risk was limited on the way.
- [Machines and operations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/operations.md): 8 lessons, OPS-n. Running many agents on real machines, and keeping the result healthy after merge.
- [Security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/security.md): 10 lessons, SEC-n. Sandboxing agents, memory safety, dependencies and data integrity.
- [Cost](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/cost.md): 9 lessons, CST-n. Tokens, money, people's time and the bill after merge.
- [Team and roles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/team.md): 6 lessons, TEM-n. Who does what when agents write most of the code.
- [Rule-based tools and AI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/tooling.md): 10 lessons, TOL-n. Splitting the work between deterministic tools and models.
- [Context and prompts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/context.md): 13 lessons, CTX-n. What goes into the model's context, and how prompts are written.
- [Many agents at once](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/orchestration.md): 6 lessons, ORC-n. Running several agents in parallel without them wrecking each other.
- [Agent failure modes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/agent-failures.md): 9 lessons, AGF-n. How agents went wrong, so a plan can expect it.
- [Human oversight](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/oversight.md): 5 lessons, OVS-n. Where people stay in the loop, and what they guard.
- [Knowledge capture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/knowledge.md): 5 lessons, KNW-n. Turning failures and logs into lasting improvements.
- [Measuring and reading results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/lessons/measurement.md): 10 lessons, MSR-n. How to read the numbers in these sources, and how to report your own.

## Cases

- [The case index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/index.md): 24 cases, one line each from its front matter (kind, from and to, AI share, evidence, the author's stake in the tools, cost, a summary), and the moves covered by the language the code was in before the move. Read it to choose cases; open only the cases you need.

## Optional

- [Everything in one file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms-full.txt): the single opt-in file that holds everything (every lesson with its sub-items, every case line, the checklist and the pitfalls), for tools that cannot follow links. About 221 KB (~57k tokens): otherwise follow the route above.
- [Pitfalls by kind of move](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/pitfalls.md): what the old stack did implicitly, and seams for moving in steps.
- [Update log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/log.md): what each update covered and changed, and why.
